posts.title: GRAMMY AWARD-WINNING PRODUCER EASY MO BEE TO LAUNCH ICONIC BEATS WITH LIVE DJ SET AND BOOK SIGNING AT TRENTON BOOK FAIR
posts.author: Matias Regis, Jr.
posts.summary: WCIP brings its Street Lit House Party experience to Trenton on October 10, featuring Easy Mo Bee and a live house music set by DJ Jonathan Lewis, co-author of House Music 101.
posts.content:
TRENTON, NJ — Grammy Award-winning producer Easy Mo Bee will bring ICONIC BEATS: Easy Mo Bee's Unforgettable Tracks for Biggie, Tupac, & Hip-Hop's Greatest to life at the Trenton Book Fair and Block Party on October 10, marking his first public book signing for the new memoir and an opportunity for audiences to experience the music behind his story. Rather than simply signing books, Easy Mo Bee will take the turntables for an approximately one-hour DJ set featuring music connected to his career and the stories explored in ICONIC BEATS. The appearance is part of WCIP's Street Lit House Party experience, which brings books, music and live cultural programming together.

EASY MO BEE BRINGS THE STORIES BEHIND THE MUSIC TO THE STAGE

In ICONIC BEATS, Easy Mo Bee opens up in his own voice about the music, moments and principles behind some of hip-hop's most unforgettable records. The book takes readers inside the making of records, the art of sampling, the politics of credit and the culture that shaped his career, including his work connected to Biggie, Tupac, Miles Davis, Busta Rhymes, Craig Mack, Alicia Keys and others. The book features a foreword by hip-hop legend Big Daddy Kane and includes a special chapter focused on Easy Mo Bee's work with Miles Davis on Doo-Bop.

"We're not bringing Easy Mo Bee to Trenton just to sit behind a table and sign books. We're bringing the stories and the music together. He'll sign ICONIC BEATS and get behind the turntables to play the records connected to his journey. Then DJ Jonathan Lewis will take us into the world of house music. That's what Street Lit House Party is about: bringing the culture in the books to life." says Wahida Clark, Founder, Wahida Clark Innovative Publishing

FROM HIP-HOP TO HOUSE MUSIC

The Trenton experience will also feature DJ Jonathan Lewis, co-author of House Music 101, with a one-hour house music set. Lewis's appearance expands the Street Lit House Party experience beyond a single author or genre, connecting the history documented in the books with the music and culture that continue to shape audiences today.

The program will also spotlight WCIP titles and authors, including House Music 101, Muqarabun and Rent Money.

Trenton Book Fair and Block Party — October 10, 2026 — Trenton, New Jersey

ABOUT WAHIDA CLARK INNOVATIVE PUBLISHING
Wahida Clark Innovative Publishing (WCIP) is an independent publishing company founded by award-winning author Wahida Clark. WCIP publishes compelling, culturally relevant books and develops opportunities that connect authors and their stories with readers and audiences through innovative publishing, marketing, media and promotional initiatives.
MEDIA CONTACT
Matias Regis, Jr. — Media Relations Specialist — Wahida Clark Innovative Publishing — pr@wahidaclarkpresents.com

posts.title: Jefferson Township Kiwanis Club Named Number One New Club in the Nation
posts.author: WAJ Editorial
posts.summary: New Jersey District Kiwanis International Governor Frank Cahill presents Yvonne Ioffredo, Treasurer of the Kiwanis Club of Jefferson Township, with a plaque recognizing the club as the number one new Kiwanis club in the nation.
posts.content:
JEFFERSON TOWNSHIP -- New Jersey District Kiwanis International Governor Frank Cahill presents Yvonne Ioffredo, Treasurer of the Kiwanis Club of Jefferson Township, with a plaque congratulating the club on achieving the highest number of member registrations at its organizational meeting in January.

Of all the clubs chartered during the service year, the Kiwanis Club of Jefferson Township ranked number one in the entire United States. Cahill's theme for his year was "Double Down with Frank," and Jefferson far exceeded the membership required to charter a new Kiwanis club. The presentation was made during the New Jersey District Kiwanis Convention, held September 17–20 at the Tropicana in Atlantic City.

Kiwanis International's mission is to empower communities to improve the world by making lasting differences in the lives of children.

For information, email fcahill@njkiwanis.org or call (973) 559-6000.

posts.title: NECANN New Jersey 2026 Recap: Inside the Atlantic City Cannabis Convention
posts.author: Bridget Papino
posts.summary: Go inside NECANN New Jersey 2026 in Atlantic City with We Are Jersey and Beast Media, including two days of panels, brands, interviews and the NECANN Cup.
posts.content:
By We Are Jersey | On-site interviews by Adrianna Bauldock | Media partners with Beast Media

Atlantic City put New Jersey Cannabis in One Room

For two packed days, the Atlantic City Convention Center became a meeting ground for the people shaping cannabis in the Garden State. NECANN New Jersey 2026 brought operators, dispensary teams, cultivators, manufacturers, educators, advocates, investors, service providers, creators and curious attendees together on September 18 and 19 for a convention that moved easily between serious business and genuine community.

We Are Jersey attended as a media partner alongside Beast Media, with Adrianna Bauldock on the floor interviewing guests, speakers, brands and vendors throughout the weekend.

The bigger takeaway for New Jersey cannabis

NECANN New Jersey 2026 made one point clear: the industry is no longer having only one conversation. Regulation still matters, but so do energy costs, banking, workforce development, science, patient education, brand identity, social equity, content, events and customer trust.

posts.title: Maithili Raelle Is Turning Self-Love Into Her Next R&B Chapter
posts.author: Minnee Martinez
posts.summary: R&B has always had a way of making personal experiences feel universal. For Maithili Raelle, that connection between personal growth and music continues to shape her emergence as one of R&B's rising voices.
posts.content:
R&B has always had a way of making personal experiences feel universal. A breakup becomes a ballad. A realization becomes an anthem. A difficult chapter becomes the song somebody else needed to hear. For Maithili Raelle, that connection between personal growth and music continues to shape her emergence as one of R&B's rising voices. The 22-year-old New Jersey-raised artist is stepping into her next chapter with "I Choose Me," featuring Hiii Siddity, a soulful new release centered around self-worth, independence and the importance of choosing yourself. But for Maithili, choosing yourself isn't necessarily about shutting the world out. It's about finally listening to yourself.

Maithili's latest release follows the momentum of "Used To Love," her breakout single that sampled Usher's "You Remind Me" and surpassed 350,000 streams. That record introduced listeners to her ability to pair soulful vocals with emotionally driven storytelling. "I Choose Me" builds on that foundation, but the perspective has changed. This time, the conversation isn't primarily about what happened with someone else. It's about what happens when you decide to prioritize yourself.

At 22, Maithili is still discovering what her sound can become. But there's already a clear throughline in her work: emotion matters. The story matters. And the person behind the voice matters just as much as the record itself.

From sampling an R&B classic to creating music that speaks directly to her own generation, Maithili is showing that evolution doesn't mean abandoning where you came from. Sometimes it means taking everything you've learned and finally making it yours. With "I Choose Me," Maithili Raelle isn't just entering another chapter. She's choosing what that chapter gets to sound like. See for yourself here at We Are Jersey Magazine! CONNECT WITH MAITHILI ON SOCIAL MEDIA: Instagram | Apple Music | Spotify | YouTube

posts.title: Latina Civic Foundation Celebrates Latina Excellence, Leadership, and Public Service During Hispanic Heritage Month
posts.author: Manuela Gaviria
posts.summary: As New Jersey celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month, the Latina Civic Foundation will mark a milestone with the inaugural Latina Excellence Breakfast on Friday, October 9, 2026, at The Rutgers Club in Piscataway.
posts.content:
PISCATAWAY, N.J. — September 15, 2026 — As New Jersey celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month and honors the contributions, achievements and leadership of its Latino community, the Latina Civic Foundation will mark a milestone of its own with the inaugural Latina Excellence Breakfast on Friday, October 9, 2026, at The Rutgers Club in Piscataway.

The event celebrates five years of the Latina Civic Foundation and a decade of advancing Latina leadership, civic engagement and public service. The breakfast will feature a historic leadership conversation with Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-09) and Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (D-11), New Jersey's first and second Latina members of Congress. Their journeys to Congress mark a significant milestone in New Jersey's political history and in the growing civic leadership of Latinas across the state.

The Latina Civic Foundation will also honor Zulima Farber, Esq., New Jersey's first Latina Attorney General, the first female partner at the prestigious law firm Lowenstein Sandler, LLP., and a co-founder of the Latina Civic Foundation.

This event will also honor other New Jersey women leaders in public service who became firsts, "Las Primeras," including M. Teresa Ruiz, Senate Majority Leader for District 29; Annette Quijano, Speaker Pro-Tempore for District 20; Wilda Diaz, former Mayor of Perth Amboy; Yolanda Garcia-Balicki, Cumberland County Commissioner; and Silvia Catalan-Culnan, Deputy Mayor of Mount Laurel Township.

"During Hispanic Heritage Month, we celebrate not only where we come from, but also the extraordinary contributions Latinas are making today," said María Del Cid-Kosso, Chair of Latina Civic Foundation.

To purchase sponsorships or tickets, visit latinacivicfoundation.org. For questions, reach out to sponsorship@latinacivicfoundation.org.
